objective: Resolve the checkout API outage and produce the postmortem with corrective actions.

decisions.text: Roll back to v2.13 immediately (done 14:20), then fix forward.
decisions.rationale: Stop the bleeding first; the v2.14 features were not urgent.

decisions.text: Keep v2.14's new checkout UI behind a feature flag on re-release.
decisions.rationale: Decouple the UI rollout from backend changes.

decisions.text: No blame on the on-call engineer.
decisions.rationale: The config change shipped unreviewed; that is a process failure, not an individual one.

evidence.claim: Root cause: the v2.14 config change cut the DB connection pool from 100 to 20; the pool exhausted under normal load.
The canary ran 5 minutes at 1% traffic — too little to surface pool exhaustion.
The config change shipped unreviewed, bundled inside the release PR.
The database was never down; the DB was fine throughout.

open_questions: Who approved bundling the config change into the release PR?
Why was the canary duration and traffic level insufficient to catch pool exhaustion?
Are there other services with silently reduced pool sizes?
next_actions: Add a connection-pool saturation alert (owner: on-call, due Oct 21).
Require separate review for config changes inside release PRs (owner: eng manager).
Load-test the canary at 10% traffic for a 30 min minimum (owner: platform).
Audit connection pool sizes across all services (owner: Priya).
